author: Jane Bellmyer
title: Cecil County Fair returns for another year - NewsBreak
text:
By Jane Bellmyer ,
1 days ago
FAIR HILL — There are two new entertainers coming to the Cecil County Fair this year: Scott’s World of Magic and All-American Pig Races.
The Cecil County Fair is set from July 24 through Aug. 1 at the Cecil County Fairgrounds on Telegraph Road near the Maryland-Delaware line.
Part of the Great American Entertainment company, the pig races will offer a collection of young pigs running on a sawdust track at the grandstands. Scott’s World of Magic features Scott and Ana, also performing at the grandstands. Sit up close if you want your chance to become part of their show.
In addition, Marty Long is Uprooted returns with his chainsaw art, as do the Mobile Glass Blowers and Blacksmiths. The items these artists create as you watch will be auctioned off to benefit the fair during the fair July 29 at 7:30 p.m. and Aug. 1 at 7 p.m.
Those auctions in 2025 helped the Cecil County Fair Board purchase some new, higher bleachers for the fair, which will bring with it additional seating.
Of course, there will be live music each night, including Gospel Music Night on July 30, and rock, classic, blues and country before the nine-day run is over.
Once again, each day at the Cecil County Fair is dedicated to a theme.
Old Time Farm Weekend is the first Saturday and Sunday, with antique tractors on display, parading and pulling. Then there’s Children’s Day, Ag Day, Military Appreciation Day, Gospel Night, 4-H Appreciation Day and Demo Derby Day.
“Ag Day will be different this year,” said Don Moore, president of the Cecil County Fair Board of Directors. “We’ll still have vendors, lunch and speakers, but it’ll only run from noon until 1:30.”
Moore said organizers noted in recent years that running the event from 10 a.m. until 2 created a hardship for many at this time of year.
Maryland Department of Agriculture is bring back its AG Trailer for the entire run of the fair.
Monday and Tuesday brings the Painted Pony Rodeo to the fair each evening. Wednesday night is the Double Figure 8 Race. Thursday, Friday and twice on Saturday is the Demolition Derby. Yes, there will be a special heat Thursday night featuring school buses. No, you are not allowed to save seats. Yes, you can purchase reserve seating .
“We’ve made some changes to the tractor pulls, added some classes,” Moore said. He said those additions are for performance and speed. “Typically it’s a 5-mile-per-hour speed limit, but some of these will have a 12-mile-per-hour limit.”
Moore said it was early May when all the available vendor spaces were filled.
“Which is a good problem to have,” he added.
One day admission is $5.50 online in advance for adults, $2.50 for senior citizens and children 6-12 years old. An unlimited entry pass is $21.50 for adults in advance and $11 for seniors and kids 6-12. Reserved seating adds $11 to the cost of each admission. Tickets at the gate are $1 more for each.
For the adrenaline junkies, the Midway at the fair will once again have specials. The cost for unlimited riding will vary from $25 to $30 depending on the day. July 28 is Buddy night. Get two unlimited arm bands for $35.
“Degeller Attractions is trying to keep prices down,” Moore said of the carnival company that has been a fixture at the fair for decades. “But with the price of fuel, there’s a little bit of adjusting on that.”
Parking is free, with free shuttle service from the parking areas around the fair grounds to the entrance.
Moore said there’s never any loss of helpful hands in the community when there’s a need to make the fair come together, including loaning heavy equipment to move components such as bleachers into place.
“We’re very, very fortunate with the business community in this county coming to help,” he said.
One component they have no control over is the weather.
“We’re hoping for low heat and no rain,” Moore said, adding “That’s what we ordered.”
